newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity seen higher, extends Monday rise.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity seen higher, extends Monday rise.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were expected to open higher Tuesday, extending Monday's gains on stronger cash prices in the West and a one-week delay in restarting the San Onofre 3 nuclear power unit in California.

In over-the-counter (OTC) business, August Palo Verde (PV) futures were quoted at $35.75-36.00 a megawatt hour (MWh) against Monday's settlement at $35.10, while August California-Oregon Border (COB) futures were talked at $23.50-23.65 versus yesterday's close at $23.16.
"It came in strong first thing this morning, but looks like it's settling down," an East Coast broker said, referring to early OTC activity.

Southern California Edison Co (SoCal Edison) said Monday it delayed the restart of its 1,080 megawatt (MW) San Onofre 3 nuclear unit by a week to July 17. Engineers needed time to replace the unit's instrument nozzles.
The unit, in San Clemente, Calif., has been offline since April 12 for refueling and maintenance.
SoCal Edison added the adjacent 1,080 MW unit 2 is still on scheduled to return to service about July 10 after being shut Jne 29 to replace its charge line check valves.
PG&E Corp's 1,073 MW Diablo Canyon 2 nuclear power unit on the central California coast achieved 75 percent power early Tuesday after being restarted this past weekend.
The unit on the central California coast restarted from a July 2 shutdown due to problems with its feedwater system. The 1,158 MW
WNP-2 nuclear power plant in Washington state hit 15 percent power early today but had not yet reconnected to the electricity grid.
Wet and cool weather is expected to stay in the Pacific Northwest into the weekend before a warming trend is forecast to kick in early next week.
Temperatures are projected to average near normal over most of the Southwest but below normal in the far northeast region and above normal in the extreme southwest area.
